question: Should `openclaw browser fill --fields-file` become a hard 1 MiB public input limit even though existing larger descriptor files will start failing?
rationale: The implementation and tests establish the proposed boundary, but only a maintainer can decide whether protecting this local CLI path warrants changing the established input-size contract.

options.title: Hold the hard cap pending policy
options.body: Keep the existing behavior until a Browser-surface owner defines an approved compatibility and resource-safety policy for larger fields files.

options.title: Approve the 1 MiB contract
options.body: Accept the runtime rejection as an intentional CLI compatibility change and merge with the documented 1 MiB limit.

recommendation.title: Hold the hard cap pending policy
recommendation.body: Keep the existing behavior until a Browser-surface owner defines an approved compatibility and resource-safety policy for larger fields files.

likelyOwner.reason: The available feature-history signal places this person near the Browser plugin architecture, so they are the best low-confidence routing candidate for the input-contract decision.
